results.content:
﻿

 Edit it yourself, or just ask Manus. Frames from the launch film above You don't need editing experience to use Video Editor. You only need to know the feel you want.

### For creators: start from your own footage

Because Video Editor runs on your desktop, it can start from the footage already on your computer. Drag videos into the chat, or tell Manus which folder they're in, and it imports them and lays them on the timeline. 

﻿ [...] Manus can make everything a video needs on the spot: shots from video models like Seedance 2.5, plus images, music, voiceover and sound effects. But what's special is the code. Manus has its own computer, enabling it to write code for motion graphics, layouts, charts and map routes, render them, screenshot the result to check it, and keep fixing what it doesn't like. I've watched it draw a grid over a frame in Python to locate pixels, and use FFmpeg to turn 24 fps footage into 120 fps so a 5x slow-motion shot stays smooth. I never taught it that. It worked these tricks out to make the video better. Generated shots and code-made visuals can share one video. For BEAT RUSH, Manus generated a dancing anime character with Seedance, then built the rhythm-game interface and beat effects in code. [...] ### Every layer is its own track

Every ingredient Manus uses, from generated shots and images to captions, motion graphics, voiceover, music and sound effects, sits on its own layer of the Video Editor timeline. You don't get a flattened MP4. You get a video you can take apart and change. 

﻿

 A vlog clip split into eight layers, 30 seconds

### For everyone: drag it yourself, or just ask Manus

You can drag, trim, rewrite captions and set volume with your mouse, like in any editor. Or tell Manus "turn the music down" or "tighten this part." Both change the same project. When you hand it back, Manus picks up from your edits instead of starting over.

results.title: Introducing Manus 2.0
results.content:
Video Editor is built for short product ads (30 to 60 seconds), AI UGC, data motion graphics, tutorials, vlogs, and motion-led videos. You don't need any editing experience.

#### Alchemy mode: AI as your creative director

﻿

Video Editor also has Alchemy mode. You start from an idea, and Manus takes on the creative direction, using video and code generation together. The jump in quality is surprisingly big: the ideas are more creative, visual details are under tighter control, the motion is more polished, and the pacing of the edit is noticeably better. When quality matters most, Alchemy mode is the one to use. You can still fine-tune the result on the timeline afterward.

#### Game Dev: Build it. Ship it. Play it together.

﻿ [...] ﻿

Say your launch ad goes out tomorrow, and Manus has already put together a first cut. It's close. You'd just like a warmer song, and you'd rather use the product shot you took yourself than the generated one.

Before, changes like that meant writing a new prompt and generating the whole video again. In Studio, Manus gives you the timeline instead. The clips, images, text, motion graphics, and audio it used are all there as separate pieces, so you can swap the song, drop in your own footage, move an animation, and export when you're happy with it.

﻿

You can also hand it back. Ask Manus to take another pass, and it works from your edits. [...] Each kind of work needs its own professional tools, but carrying every capability into every task makes the same work slower and more expensive. So Studio brings in only what your project calls for, keeping Manus's context focused on the work at hand. In this release, Studio gets major upgrades for both everyday work and professional creation: documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, and slides, as well as websites, code, games, and video. And for video and games, where the bar is especially high, we're introducing two all-new professional environments: Video Editor and Game Dev.

#### Video Editor: Make the first cut in minutes. Keep the final cut for yourself.

Clips, images, text, motion graphics and audio appear as separate pieces that users can swap, move or replace with their own footage. Manus can then take another pass that works from those edits.

Manus said the tool targets short product ads of 30 to 60 seconds, AI-generated user content, data motion graphics, tutorials, vlogs, and motion-led videos.

Video Editor also includes Alchemy mode, in which Manus handles creative direction using video and code generation together. The company claimed the mode brings better ideas, tighter control of visual detail, more polished motion and improved pacing, and said users can still fine-tune results on the timeline. [...] Users configure a workflow through a single prompt. “Just tell Manus in a single prompt what to watch and what to do next, and it sets up and runs the workflow,” the company said.

The desktop app has been renamed Manus Studio, which Manus describes as “a shared workspace for people and AI.” Studio loads only the tools a project requires, which the company says keeps Manus focused on the task at hand.

The release upgrades Studio for documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, slides, websites and code. It also adds two new professional environments, Video Editor and Game Dev.

Video Editor addresses a limitation of earlier versions, where changing a generated video meant writing a new prompt and regenerating the whole clip. Now, the company said, “Manus gives you the timeline instead.” [...] Singapore – Manus has released Manus 2.0, an overhaul that introduces a new agent architecture, a desktop workspace for video and game creation, and a standalone app for personal AI agents. The company, which operates under Meta, announced the update in a blog post.

The company said the release goes beyond a routine upgrade. Manus 2.0 is not a version update. It’s a new architecture, new products, and new capabilities built around a fundamental question: what should the next generation of Manus look like?

At the core of the update is Cascade, which Manus describes as the latest iteration of its in-house agent harness. According to the company, it keeps a project light from the start and brings in specialised capabilities only when the work needs them.
